rulings: The only attack considered for the "Festival Lead" Ability is the attack printed directly on the Pokémon card with the Ability ("this Pokémon may use an attack it has twice"). Cards that grant the Pokémon additional attacks such as Technical Machine s are not considered for "Festival Lead".

If a player's Pokémon with "Festival Lead" has 1 Energy attached to it and uses an attack on the opponent's Active Pokémon with  attached, and the Energy is moved to the player's Benched Pokémon, the Attacking Pokémon with Festival Lead cannot attack the second time, as the Energy requirement is no longer satisfied.
For interactions between a Pokémon with the "Festival Lead" Ability and  from , which has the "Midnight Fluttering" Ability that shuts down the opposing Active Pokémon's Ability:

*If a player uses a "Festival Lead" Pokémon to Knock Out their opponent's Active Pokémon and the opponent sends out Flutter Mane with the "Midnight Fluttering" Ability as a replacement Active Pokémon, the "Festival Lead" Ability is immediately removed and the player may not attack a second time.

*If a player uses a "Festival Lead" Pokémon to Knock Out their opponent's Active Flutter Mane with the "Midnight Fluttering" Ability, the "Festival Lead" Ability reactivates upon the Flutter Mane being Knocked Out, and thus the "Festival Lead" Pokémon may attack a second time.

This allows it to be used from the Bench, allowing players to use multiple Slowking to further reduce the odds of a  being successfully played to as low as to 1 in 16. Slowking became extremely popular, with games often coming down to who could play multiple Slowking first to shut their opponent out of search and draw power and clog their draws, all while being essentially shielded from attacks due to being on the Bench. Due to its widely perceived negative influence on gameplay, the card was banned from the  at the end of 2002.

rulings: For interactions between the "Resolute Heart"  when Pikachu ex is at full HP, the "Calamity Storm" attack of  from , and the  :

*If Lively Stadium is in play, such that an opponent's Pikachu ex's HP becomes 230, and the player uses Roaring Moon ex's Calamity Storm attack and discards the Lively Stadium using the attack's effect, Pikachu ex receives 220 damage. On this condition, since Pikachu ex has 230 HP and receives 220 damage, its Resolute Heart Ability is no longer in effect (as its HP is no longer considered full). Thus, once Lively Stadium is removed from play, Pikachu ex will have its HP reduced to 200, and with 220 damage on it, it will be Knocked Out.

*However, if damage done by the Calamity Storm attack is increased to 230 or more (eg. using ), Resolute Heart becomes in effect as the Calamity Storm damage would have Knocked Out the Pikachu ex. Thus, once Lively Stadium is discarded, Pikachu ex remains in play with a remaining HP of 10 (effectively having 190 damage on it once all the effects have resolved).

rulings: For interactions between the "Resolute Heart"  when Pikachu ex is at full HP, the "Calamity Storm" attack of  from , and the  :

*If Lively Stadium is in play, such that an opponent's Pikachu ex's HP becomes 230, and the player uses Roaring Moon ex's Calamity Storm attack and discards the Lively Stadium using the attack's effect, Pikachu ex receives 220 damage. On this condition, since Pikachu ex has 230 HP and receives 220 damage, its Resolute Heart Ability is no longer in effect (as its HP is no longer considered full). Thus, once Lively Stadium is removed from play, Pikachu ex will have its HP reduced to 200, and with 220 damage on it, it will be Knocked Out.

*However, if damage done by the Calamity Storm attack is increased to 230 or more (eg. using ), Resolute Heart becomes in effect as the Calamity Storm damage would have Knocked Out the Pikachu ex. Thus, once Lively Stadium is discarded, Pikachu ex remains in play with a remaining HP of 10 (effectively having 190 damage on it once all the effects have resolved).

Even if a Pokémon is immune to damage from Nullifying Zero (eg. a  that has protection from attack damage while on the Bench), the player still flips a coin for that Pokémon.
All damage from Nullifying Zero is placed simultaneously after each Pokémon has been checked via the coin flips.

If that Pokémon was evolved in this way, that player may search their deck for a Stage 2 Pokémon that evolves from that Pokémon and put it onto that Pokémon to evolve it. Then, that player shuffles their deck. (Players can’t evolve a Basic Pokémon during their first turn or a Basic Pokémon that was put into play this turn.)
rulings: Players may use Grand Tree to evolve a  into a  that has no  Evolution. They may not use Grand Tree if none of their Pokémon in play are capable of evolving into a Stage 1 Pokémon.

For Pokémon with  that allow it to be evolved on the first turn or on the turn it is played (eg.  with "Adaptive Evolution" or  with "Boosted Evolution"), Grand Tree may not be used to evolve them on the first turn or on the turn those Pokémon are played.
Grand Tree cannot be used to evolve , as its "Rainbow DNA"  states that the Evolution card has to be played on top of the Eevee ex from the hand.

Using Grand Tree to evolve a Pokémon counts as evolving it for the turn, thus the Pokémon can't evolve further on the same turn, as each Pokémon can only evolve once during a player's turn. For instance, a player using Grand Tree on a  to evolve it into a  may not then evolve it into a  from hand, as that Charmeleon is considered to have already evolved for that turn.

name: Area Zero Underdepths
effect_text:
Each player who has any Tera Pokémon in play can have up to 8 Pokémon on their Bench.

If a player no longer has any Tera Pokémon in play, that player discards Pokémon from their Bench until they have 5. When this card leaves play, both players discard Pokémon from their Bench until they have 5, and the player who played this card discards first.
rulings: Area Zero Underdepths's effect of expanding the Bench from 5 to 8 applies to each player's in-play zone if and only if they have a  in play. Thus, when Area Zero Underdepths is in play, the following rules apply:

* If a player has no Tera Pokémon in play and 4 Benched Pokémon, and they use a card effect that allows them to put more than 1 Pokémon to the Bench at once (eg. 's "Form Ranks" attack), they can only put 1 Pokémon to the Bench even if the Pokémon being put to the Bench is a Tera Pokémon. Only once the Tera Pokémon is in play does Area Zero Underdepths's effect apply for that player.

* If a player has a Tera Pokémon in the Active Spot and more than 5 Benched non-Tera Pokémon, and their Active Tera Pokémon is Knocked Out or otherwise removed from play, the player must discard their Benched Pokémon down to 5 first before promoting a new Active Pokémon, such that once the effect resolves, the player will have an Active Pokémon and 4 Benched Pokémon.

* If a player has a damaged Benched Tera Evolution Pokémon and more than 5 Benched Pokémon (including the Tera Pokémon), and if their opponent uses  to devolve the player's Tera Pokémon, the player discards their Benched Pokémon down to 5 first before resolving any other effects. Thus, the player may choose to discard the damaged Benched Pokémon that was just devolved; if the damaged Pokémon is discarded in this way, it is not considered Knocked Out, and the opponent does not take any Prize cards for it.

Replacing an Area Zero Underdepths in play with  and vice versa will not change the number of Bench slots on either players' in-play zone, so long as all the requirements for either Stadium are fulfilled.

Using  to switch an "" card in play with an Ogerpon ex card in the discard pile does not nullify the effect of Area Zero Underdepths; the effect of Area Zero Underdepths continues instantaneously with the new Ogerpon ex.

name: Lively Stadium
effect_text: Each Basic Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent’s) gets +30 HP.
rulings: For interactions between Lively Stadium, the "Calamity Storm" attack of  from , and the "Resolute Heart"  of  from  when the Pikachu ex is at full HP:

*If Lively Stadium is in play, such that an opponent's Pikachu ex's HP becomes 230, and the player uses Roaring Moon ex's Calamity Storm attack and discards the Lively Stadium using the attack's effect, Pikachu ex receives 220 damage. On this condition, since Pikachu ex has 230 HP and receives 220 damage, its Resolute Heart Ability is no longer in effect (as its HP is no longer considered full). Thus, once Lively Stadium is removed from play, Pikachu ex will have its HP reduced to 200, and with 220 damage on it, it will be Knocked Out.

*However, if damage done by the Calamity Storm attack is increased to 230 or more (eg. using ), Resolute Heart becomes in effect as the Calamity Storm damage would have Knocked Out the Pikachu ex. Thus, once Lively Stadium is discarded, Pikachu ex remains in play with a remaining HP of 10 (effectively having 190 damage on it once all the effects have resolved).

name: Battle Cage
effect_text: Prevent all damage counters from being placed on Benched Pokémon (both yours and your opponent’s) by effects of attacks and Abilities from the opponent’s Pokémon. (Damage from attacks is still taken.)
rulings: If Battle Cage is in play, and a player uses any attack or  that moves damage counters from any Pokémon to the opponent's Benched Pokémon, the damage counters will be removed from the source Pokémon but won't be placed on the target Benched Pokémon due to the Stadium's effect, ultimately removing the damage from play altogether. If the player targets the opponent's Active Pokémon, the attack or Ability will place the damage counters as usual.

* For example, with Battle Cage in play, a player can use 's "Adrena-Brain" Ability to remove 3 damage counters from their Pokémon, but the damage counters cannot then be placed on the opponent's Benched Pokémon.

* If Battle Cage is in play and a player uses 's "Strange Hacking" attack to move damage counters from the opponent's Pokémon to their Benched Pokémon, Battle Cage will prevent the damage counters from being placed and the damage counters are simply removed, even though the damage counters originated from the opponent's Pokémon.

If Battle Cage is in play, and a player uses  or 's "Cursed Blast" Ability and targets the opponent's Benched Pokémon, the Pokémon using the Ability will still be Knocked Out even if no damage counters can be placed.
